titre: Jefferson and Burr, 73 Votes Each: The Election of 1800 and the Twelfth Amendment
accroche: In 1800, presidential electors do not distinguish president from vice president on their ballots. Two candidates from the same side end up tied.
contenu_vulgarise:
## Two names on a ballot

The American Constitution of 1787 does not provide one ballot for president and another for vice president. Each elector is to “vote by Ballot for two Persons.” The one who gets the most votes, if he has a majority, becomes president. The vice president is, after the choice of the president, the one with the most votes among the rest. If two candidates have a majority and the same number of votes, the House of Representatives chooses between them.

This mechanism ignores parties. In 1800, there are two. The Democratic-Republicans, behind Thomas Jefferson, run Aaron Burr as their candidate for vice president. But each Republican elector must write down two names, and all of them write the same two.

## Seventy-three apiece

The count gives 73 votes to Jefferson, 73 to Burr, 65 to John Adams, 64 to Charles Pinckney, and one to John Jay, out of 138 electors. The majority is 70: Jefferson and Burr both have it, tied. It is therefore up to the House to choose, with one vote per state. There are then sixteen states, and nine are needed.

The House that votes is the outgoing one, elected in 1798: the Federalists hold sixty seats there against forty-six. It could prefer Burr to Jefferson, who is nonetheless the designated candidate of the winning side. It begins voting on February 11, 1801, during a snowstorm in Washington. Over the first thirty-five ballots, Jefferson gets eight states. On February 17, on the thirty-sixth, James Bayard and his allies from Maryland and Vermont change position, and Jefferson wins with ten states.

## The fix

Congress adopts the Twelfth Amendment on December 9, 1803, and the states ratify it on June 15, 1804. It replaces part of Article II: electors now vote by separate ballots for president and for vice president.

The fix concerns the form of the ballot, not the role of the House: with two separate ballots, a running mate can no longer rival his presidential candidate simply by receiving the same votes. The 1787 text had not been written for organized camps, and the election of 1800 showed it by making the outcome depend on an outgoing House dominated by the losing camp.

repere.texte: Election of 1800: Jefferson 73 votes, Burr 73, Adams 65, Pinckney 64, Jay 1. In the House of Representatives, Jefferson wins eight states in the first thirty-five ballots, then ten states on the thirty-sixth, on February 17, 1801.

carte.punch: In 1800, two candidates from the same side are tied: the ballot ignored the vice presidency.
carte.idee: Each elector voted for two names, without specifying which was meant for the presidency. In 1800, Jefferson and Burr get 73 votes each. The House takes 36 ballots to break the tie, and the Twelfth Amendment (1804) separates the two ballots.

quiz.question: Why does the election of 1800 end in a tie between Jefferson and Burr?
choix: Because Republican electors voted for the same two names, with no way to designate which one was meant for the presidency
Because Federalist electors all abstained, leaving the Republican votes tied
Because the South Carolina vote count was annulled by the House
Because the 1787 Constitution required a separate vote for each office, which the electors ignored
quiz.explication: Each elector had to write down two names, without specifying president or vice president. Republican electors wrote the same two. The separate vote came only with the Twelfth Amendment of 1804, so it could not have been ignored. The Federalists did vote (Adams 65 votes, Pinckney 64), and no count was annulled.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How many states did the House of Representatives count in 1800, and how many were needed to win?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: There were then sixteen states, and nine were needed: Jefferson gets ten states on the thirty-sixth ballot, above the required threshold.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the Twelfth Amendment, adopted in 1803 and ratified in 1804, change?
choix: It abolished the House vote in case of an electoral tie
It lowered the majority required in the House from nine to seven states
It established separate ballots for president and vice president
It gave electors the right to vote for three people instead of two
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Twelfth Amendment replaces part of Article II: presidential electors now vote by separate ballots for president and for vice president.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why could the House that decided the election, in theory, prefer Burr to Jefferson?
choix: Because it was made up half of Republicans and half of Federalists
Because it was the outgoing House, elected in 1798, with a Federalist majority
Because Burr had received more electoral votes than Jefferson
Because the Constitution gave the Senate the power to reject the House's choice
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The House that votes is the one elected in 1798, where the Federalists hold sixty seats against forty-six for the Republicans, Jefferson's camp.
